cards.front: What should you know about ao6 requirement?
cards.back: Accurate and effective punctuation isn't just about correctness - it's about using punctuation deliberately to create effects and control your reader's experience.

cards.front: What should you know about tip?
cards.back: The colon acts like a spotlight, directing attention to what comes next. Use it to make important statements stand out.

cards.front: What should you know about think of it this way?
cards.back: A semi-colon is stronger than a comma but weaker than a full stop. It shows ideas are connected but distinct.

cards.front: What should you know about dash tip?
cards.back: An em dash (—) is longer than a hyphen (-). In exams, you can use two hyphens (--) if you can't make an em dash.

cards.front: What should you know about warning?
cards.back: Use exclamation marks sparingly. Overusing them weakens their impact and looks immature. One per piece of writing is often enough.

cards.front: What should you know about punctuation for effect exam strategy?
cards.back: Using punctuation for deliberate effect lifts your AO6 mark from Level 3 to Level 4. It shows sophistication and control. Accuracy first: Ensure all basic punctuation is correct before attempting sophisticated marks. A missing full stop costs more than an absent semi-colon gains. Three marks to include: Aim to use at least one colon (for a dramatic reveal or list), one semi-colon (to link related ideas), and one dash or ellipsis (for dramatic effect) in every piece of creative writing. In transactional writing: Use colons to introduce explanations or lists, and semi-colons in complex lists. Th
Dramatic reveal, emphasis (e.g. Important statements, lists)
Links related ideas (e.g. Connecting sentences, complex lists)
Strong pause, interruption (e.g. Drama, emphasis, breaks)

cards.front: What does It was cold, dark, dangerous. mean?
cards.back: It was cold, dark, and dangerous. (e.g. Oxford comma clarifies lists)
"Stop," she said. (e.g. Comma inside speech marks)

cards.front: What does She ran; and hid. mean?
cards.back: She ran and hid. (e.g. No semi-colon needed with 'and')

cards.front: What does He was tall; dark; handsome. mean?
cards.back: He was tall, dark, and handsome. (e.g. Use commas for simple lists)
